title: Smoke Inspector: Sequential API readiness, model cold-load timing, and core-sanity checks
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a compact, deterministic 'Smoke Inspector' that runs automatically after a Private (VPC) deployment to validate API readiness, measure model cold-load latency, and exercise core sanity checks before marking the deployment as ready.

Scope: The inspector should run as a single-run job after orchestration completes and must: (1) validate control-plane API handshake and authentication, (2) run a series of lightweight model load scenarios (cold-start and hot-start timing), (3) run functional smoke prompts to assert generation correctness and deterministic outputs for known seeds, (4) emit structured metrics to the Console and a short human-readable report to the deployment log.

Out of scope: full load or performance benchmarking, long-duration stability runs, and large-scale KV-cache priming. These remain separate test suites.

Why this ticket: Existing post-deploy checks are fragmented (separate probes for API and model warmup). Operators requested a single, ordered check that surfaces specific failure signals (auth failure, slow model init, incorrect model variant, routing mismatches) with clear remediation hints.
acceptance_criteria: Smoke Inspector runs automatically after Terraform apply finishes and returns a non-zero exit code on any critical failure.
Inspector validates API handshake (TLS + signed token), returns 200 for /v1/health and performs a token-introspection call to the control plane.
Cold-load timing recorded: first-token latency for a reference prompt is captured and compared against advisory thresholds; findings sent to console dashboard and deployment log.
Model load verification: attempt model load with a small prompt, check model version and hash against deployment manifest; mismatch triggers error with remediation link.
Functional smoke prompts: 5 deterministic prompts (with seeding) run and responses matched against golden baseline signatures; failures flagged with diff and example outputs.
Structured metrics emitted under metric tags smoke_inspector.* and a short summary uploaded to the deployment artifact store (link printed in logs).
Operator runbook link present in failure output and PR providing remediation steps linked in the inspector logs.
Automated retries: transient network errors are retried up to 2 times with exponential backoff; persistent errors fail fast after retries.
Inspector completes within configurable timeout (default 8 minutes) and exits with 0 on success.
steps: Design API: define inspector execution phases (control-plane-check, token-introspect, model-cold-load, functional-smoke, metrics-publish).
Create a lightweight CLI binary (Go) that can be dropped into the post-deploy job container; param driven by env and flags.
Implement control-plane handshake and token-introspect; reuse existing SDK auth helpers to avoid duplicate secrets handling.
Integrate model loader probe: call private inference endpoint with small prompt, capture first-token and total-token timings, retrieve model metadata (name, version, checksum).
Add deterministic smoke prompts with seeding and baseline signatures; store baselines in a small JSON asset under infra/inspector/baselines.
Emit structured metrics to Console via the metrics ingestion endpoint and write a one-page summary to the deployment artifact bucket.
Create Terraform job resource (module) that runs the inspector as a post-deploy null_resource/local-exec or native job runner, with configurable retry and timeout.
Write operator runbook snippet and integrate link into inspector failure payloads; add a flag to skip on-demand for expedited rollbacks.
Add unit and integration tests (mock control-plane, a shimbed model server) and a GitHub Actions workflow to run inspector unit tests on PRs.
Open PR against infra/terraform-modules to wire the job into the standard VPC deployment pipeline and add a feature flag for gradual rollout.
comments: 2026-02-10 - Asha Patel: Created ticket. Initial design meeting scheduled with Infra and Runtime teams to align on model metadata contract.
2026-02-17 - Diego Morales: Implemented initial control-plane handshake prototype. Observed token introspection mismatch on staging (fixed by using new admin token scope).
2026-02-25 - Maya Chen: Reviewed smoke prompt list; removed prompts that relied on web-scrape facts to avoid flakiness. Added deterministic seeding.

2026-03-02 - Diego Morales: Model cold-load probe implemented; first-token latency captured. On a g4dn-equivalent node first-token median ~420ms which is within advisory thresholds. Pushed draft CLI to infra branch.
2026-03-08 - SRE (review): Suggested adding exponential backoff for transient DNS errors and making thresholds configurable per deployment class (dev/staging/prod).
2026-03-10 - Diego Morales: Added metrics emission and artifact upload. Running integration tests in CI. Marking In Progress -> awaiting infra module PR review.
notes: Decision: Use a small Go binary rather than Python to minimize runtime surface and avoid Python dependency conflicts in constrained job runners.
Trade-off: Keeping baselines in S3 simplifies updates but requires a versioning discipline; will add checksum validation on load to avoid silent drift.
Alternative considered: Integrating inspector into existing canary probes. Rejected because inspector needs ordered semantics and richer model assertions not present in the current probe runner.
Follow-up: After merging, schedule a retro to evaluate false-positive rate over the next two weekly deploys and adjust thresholds accordingly.
